cyber-dragon.gamePlan: Cyber Dragon is a Machine deck built around the new Cyber support: you reveal Cyber Dragon or Cyber Jormungardr for the skill, add small Cyber Dragons, and use Cyber Dragon Core, Cyberdark Realm and Cyberdark Chimera to search Power Bond, I:P Masquerena and the Rank 5 and Fusion Monsters of the Extra Deck. The goal is a board with an omni-negate (Cyber Dragon Infinity), a monster negate (Chronomaly Vimana), a spell/trap negate (Heosvarog the Mechanical Dawn) and I:P Masquerena into S:P Little Knight on the opponent's turn, with Power Bond into Cyber End Dragon (8000 ATK) as the finisher for turn 2. The guide follows two creators: Build 1 (YRalps) plays 30 cards with eight hand traps, and Build 2 (IgnisterPRC) plays 24 cards and no hand traps, in a more combo-heavy list. The Alternatives tab shows what changes.
strengths: A very good search engine: Cyber Emergency ×3, Cyber Repair Plant ×3, Core and the skill find the pieces of the combo.
Many different interactions in the Extra Deck: an omni-negate, a monster negate, a spell/trap negate, and S:P Little Knight on the opponent's turn.
Power Bond into Cyber End Dragon gives a strong finisher with piercing damage.
It is an anime deck and the creators say it is fun and good for starters.
weaknesses: The deck locks you into Machine monsters when you use some effects (Cyber Jormungardr, Herz, Nachster), which limits what else you can summon.
After the skill's third effect you cannot activate Spells other than Polymerization and Power Bond until Cyber End Dragon is summoned.
Power Bond costs you 4000 Life Points for Cyber End Dragon, so it is risky.
Build 2 has no hand traps, and both builds depend on the skill, which can only be used once per Duel.

cards.name: Cyber Dragon
cards.note: The namesake. If only your opponent controls a monster you can Special Summon it from your hand. Several cards in the deck count as "Cyber Dragon" in the Graveyard (Core, Nachster, Herz, Cyberdark Wurm), which matters for Power Bond and the skill. Build 1 plays 3, Build 2 plays 2.

cards.name: Cyber Jormungardr
cards.note: Cannot be Normal Summoned. If your opponent controls a monster it Special Summons itself, then takes a Cyber Dragon from your deck and either Special Summons or equips it; and it can return a Cyber Dragon to your hand to add Polymerization. You can reveal it for the skill. Both builds play 3.

cards.name: Cyber Dragon Core
cards.note: Level 2 you add with the skill. When Normal Summoned it adds a Cyber Spell/Trap, and from the Graveyard it brings a Cyber Dragon when only the opponent has a monster. Build 1 plays 2, Build 2 plays 3.

cards.name: Cyber Dragon Nachster
cards.note: Special Summons itself by discarding a monster, and when it is summoned it brings back a Machine with 2100 ATK or DEF from the Graveyard (Cyber Dragon, Cyberdark Wurm or Jormungardr). The creators say it is the card that makes the turn-one combo run, so you want it in hand. Both builds play 1.

cards.name: Cyber Dragon Herz
cards.note: Level 1 you can add with the skill. It becomes Level 5 when Special Summoned (for the Rank 5 Xyz) and, when sent to the Graveyard, adds another Cyber Dragon. Both builds play 1.

cards.name: Cyberdark Wurm
cards.note: Once per Duel it Special Summons itself from your hand or Graveyard by sending a Cyber Dragon, then adds a Cyber Spell/Trap from your Graveyard. It counts as "Cyber Dragon" in the Graveyard. Both builds play 1.

cards.name: Cyberdark Chimera
cards.note: Level 4 that the Realm lets you summon. It discards a Spell/Trap to add Power Bond and allows a Graveyard banish as Fusion Material this turn; sent to the Graveyard, it sends a Cyberdark monster from the deck. Both builds play 1.

cards.name: Jizukiru, the Star Destroying Kaiju
cards.note: Kaiju that you can fetch with Cyber Repair Plant. It removes an opponent's monster, and fits the machine lock because it is a LIGHT Machine. Both builds play 1.

cards.name: Cyber Emergency
cards.note: The consistency spell: it adds a LIGHT Machine that cannot be Normal Summoned (like Jormungardr) or a Cyber Dragon. If the opponent negates it, you can discard a card to add it back. Both builds play 3.

cards.name: Cyber Repair Plant
cards.note: With a Cyber Dragon in the Graveyard it adds a LIGHT Machine monster from your deck (and, with 3 Cyber Dragons in the Graveyard, shuffles one back too). The creator of Build 2 uses it to fetch a Kaiju as a tech. Both builds play 3.

cards.name: Cyberdark Realm
cards.note: Continuous Spell: when activated it adds a Cyberdark monster, and it gives you an extra Normal Summon for a Cyberdark monster. Use it to bring Cyberdark Chimera. Both builds play 1.

cards.name: Power Bond
cards.note: Fusion Summons a Machine Fusion Monster with its ATK doubled (Cyber End Dragon becomes 8000 ATK), but you take damage equal to the ATK gained in the End Phase. The creators call it risky: use it when the damage will not decide the duel. Both builds play 1.

cards.name: Polymerization
cards.note: Fusion for the deck, and one of the only Spells you can still activate after the skill's third effect. Cyber Jormungardr can fetch it. Both builds play 1.

cards.name: Cyberload Fusion
cards.note: Quick-Play Spell that Fusion Summons a Fusion Monster that lists a Cyber Dragon by shuffling the materials from your field and banished cards, but your other monsters cannot attack. Only Build 2 plays it.

cards.name: Cyber Revsystem
cards.note: Only Build 2 plays it (I identified this slot from the card on the creator's deck screen): it Special Summons a Cyber Dragon from your hand or Graveyard and it cannot be destroyed by card effects.

cards.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
cards.note: Stops decks that make many Summons in one turn. Only Build 1 plays it (3 copies).

cards.name: Droll & Lock Bird
cards.note: Stops the opponent's search turn. Only Build 1 plays it (3 copies).

cards.name: Mulcharmy Fuwalos
cards.note: Hand trap that draws a card each time the opponent Special Summons from the Deck or Extra Deck. Only Build 1 plays it (2 copies).

cards.name: Cyber End Dragon
cards.note: Fusion of 3 Cyber Dragons with piercing damage. With Power Bond it has 8000 ATK, and the skill's third effect lets you use your Spells again once it is Special Summoned. Both builds play it.

cards.name: Chimeratech Rampage Dragon
cards.note: Fusion of 2 or more Cyber Dragons: when Fusion Summoned it destroys Spells/Traps (up to the number of materials) and can attack several times by sending LIGHT Machines from the deck to the Graveyard. Both builds play it.

cards.name: Chimeratech Megafleet Dragon
cards.note: Special Summoned from the Extra Deck by sending a Cyber Dragon and monsters in the Extra Monster Zone (yours or the opponent's). It breaks a board without the opponent being able to respond. Both builds play it, and the creator of Build 1 notes the Machine lock gets in its way.

cards.name: Heosvarog the Mechanical Dawn
cards.note: Fusion of 2 LIGHT Machines that negates a Spell/Trap activation (banishing a LIGHT Machine or 2 from the Graveyard) and recovers a Fusion Spell on your next Standby Phase. It is a spell/trap negate for the opponent's turn. Both builds play it.

cards.name: Cyber Dragon Infinity
cards.note: Rank 6 Xyz made with Cyber Dragon Nova: once per turn it detaches a material to negate an activation and destroy it, and it takes monsters as materials. The omni-negate of the deck. Both builds play it.

cards.name: Cyber Dragon Nova
cards.note: Rank 5 Xyz made with 2 Level 5 Machines. It detaches a material to Special Summon a Cyber Dragon from the Graveyard, gains 2100 ATK when you banish a Cyber Dragon, and lets you make Cyber Dragon Infinity on top of it. Both builds play it.

cards.name: Chronomaly Vimana
cards.note: Rank 5 Xyz that negates a monster effect by detaching 2 materials and can steal an Xyz's ATK from the Graveyard. It is the monster negate. Both builds play it.

cards.name: I:P Masquerena
cards.note: Link-2 made with two non-Link monsters. On the opponent's turn it can Link Summon again, for example S:P Little Knight. Both builds play it.

cards.name: S:P Little Knight
cards.note: Link-2 made with I:P Masquerena on the opponent's turn: it banishes a card and can banish two monsters in response to an effect. Both builds play it.

skill.name: The Eye of the United Dragon
skill.trigger: Effect 1 happens once at the start of the duel (nothing for you to do). Effects 2 and 3 can each be used once per duel, and only if your deck holds 15 or more Dark Magician cards and cards that mention it.
skill.enabler: Effect 2 needs Timaeus the United Dragon in your hand: shuffle 1 other card from your hand into your deck, Timaeus is played from your hand, and you add 2 Dark Magician cards. Illusion of Chaos and Preparation of Rites (which searches Illusion of Chaos) are ways to get Timaeus. Effect 3 needs you to control "Dark Magician" or your opponent to control a monster: it plays Dark Magician or Dark Magician Girl from your deck face-down and gives you The Eye of Timaeus.

adds.note: Added to your hand from outside your deck when you use effect 3.

dark-magician.gamePlan: Everything starts from Timaeus the United Dragon: if you hold it (or Illusion of Chaos or Preparation of Rites to fetch it) the skill turns the hand into a full combo, which the creator calls a one-card combo. Play Magician's Rod, use Illusion Magic to bring Dark Magician cards to your hand, fuse the Dragon Knight, use the skill's second effect for The Dark Magicians, and keep the extra cards for later. You finish with a monster that negates, one that flips opposing monsters face-down, two Magician Navigations in the Graveyard that negate Spells and Traps, and The Gaze of Timaeus ready to bring Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon in on the opponent's turn. If you miss Dark Magical Curtain, play extra Magician's Rod and Preparation of Rites; with only one Curtain you are still fine, because the combo searches it.
strengths: A one-card combo: with Timaeus (or a way to get it) in hand the skill builds the rest.
Soul Servant, Dark Magical Circle and Illusion of Chaos let you put cards back in your deck, so the combo is hard to brick.
It ends with several negates and a monster that resists the opponent's effects, and the creator rates it as good enough for King of Games.
weaknesses: Hand traps (D.D. Crow on the Graveyard, Droll & Lock Bird) can cut parts of the combo; keep a second Soul Servant as a safety net.
The order matters: the Dragon Knight goes in a main Monster Zone and The Dark Magicians in the Extra Monster Zone.
It is based on one creator's video and his own replays, and the opponents' answers in the replays vary.

Put the Dragon Knight in a MAIN Monster Zone, not the Extra Monster Zone: the next steps need the Extra Monster Zone free. The Dragon Knight is treated as Dark Magician, which turns on the skill's effect 3, and it protects your Spells and Traps from the opponent's effects.

steps.reason: This is the skill's effect 3: it gives you Dark Magician Girl as fusion material and a free fusion Spell, both without using up any cards from your hand.

Use The Eye of Timaeus on the face-down Dark Magician Girl to Fusion Summon The Dark Magicians. Put it in the EXTRA Monster Zone (the creator stresses this): that is where it waits before it becomes the Xyz monster later.

Activate Soul Servant to put Magician Navigation (a Dark Magician card) on top of your deck. Because you activated a Spell, The Dark Magicians can draw 1 card, and it draws that Navigation. A Trap you draw this way can be activated the same turn. In the replay the opponent banished this Soul Servant from the Graveyard with D.D. Crow, which does not matter because you hold a second copy.

Activate Magician Navigation: Special Summon Dark Magician from your hand, then Special Summon Summoner Monk (a Level 4 DARK Spellcaster) from your deck. Navigation will sit in your Graveyard to negate a Spell or Trap on the opponent's turn.

You have activated a Spell/Trap this turn, so you can Special Summon Dark Magician of Destruction from your Extra Deck by banishing a Level 6 or higher DARK Spellcaster you control (the Dark Magician). Its search adds Dark Magical Curtain.

Dark Magician of Destruction and The Dark Magicians are both Level 8, so Xyz Summon Number 90: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Lord with them. It will negate a monster effect on the opponent's turn and it takes The Dark Magicians' place in the Extra Monster Zone.
Summoner Monk discards a Spell (the spare Soul Servant) to Special Summon a Level 4 monster from your deck: take Chronicle Sorceress. The summoned monster cannot attack, which does not matter here.

Dark Magician is in your Graveyard and it is DARK, so Chronicle Sorceress can send 1 Dark Magician card from your deck to the Graveyard. Send the second Magician Navigation: it is a second Spell/Trap negate waiting for the opponent's turn.

Summoner Monk and Chronicle Sorceress are two Level 4 DARK monsters, so Xyz Summon Evilswarm Nightmare. It can flip a monster the opponent Special Summons face-down. This is the creator's favourite, but the two Level 4 monsters can become any other Level 4 DARK Xyz or Link monster you prefer.

Activate Dark Magical Curtain: you Special Summon a Dark Magician from your deck (the opponent also gets to Special Summon a DARK Spellcaster, and neither side can use those monsters' effects this turn). Because it is a real Dark Magician you add a Spell/Trap that mentions it: The Gaze of Timaeus.

Banish the Soul Servant in your Graveyard to draw cards equal to the number of different Dark Magician and Dark Magician Girl cards on the field and in the Graveyards (here 2: Dark Magician and Dark Magician Girl). Your deck is thin by now, so you are likely to draw useful cards.

The creator happened to draw Magician's Salvation; activating it also Sets Eternal Soul directly from your deck. Eternal Soul makes your Dark Magicians unaffected by the opponent's card effects once it is face-up. This step depends on your draws: with other cards, this part is your own choice.

Set The Gaze of Timaeus. During the opponent's turn it Fusion Summons Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon (using the Dark Magician on your field), which negates one more activation. The creator sums up the finished turn: 1 monster effect negate, 2 face-down flips, 2 Spell/Trap negates and 1 negate of anything.

Keep Magician Navigation in the Graveyard for the opponent's turn: it banishes itself to negate a Spell/Trap. Put the Dragon Knight in a main Monster Zone and The Dark Magicians in the Extra Monster Zone.

elemental-hero.gamePlan: This is the Elemental HERO deck updated with the new Elemental HERO Thunder Giant - Voltic Thunder, a fusion made from any 2 HERO with different Attributes that destroys every other card on the field when the opponent has more cards than you. Reveal Spirit of Neos or Miracle Ejector for the skill, take Polymerization, search with E - Emergency Call and Stratos, and fuse Voltic Thunder to wipe the board (a turn two the deck did not have before). Super Polymerization (which the skill lets you use the turn it is Set) protects the play. The old plan is still there: Favorite Contact and Neos fusions (Aqua Neos, Marine Neos) destroy cards in the opponent's hand. The creator reached Legend 5 with 14 wins in a row.
strengths: Thunder Giant - Voltic Thunder is easy to make (any 2 HERO with different Attributes) and clears the opponent's whole board, which fixes the deck's old weak turn two.
The skill gives Polymerization and sets Super Polymerization, which cannot be responded to and can be used the turn it is Set.
Many searchers (E - Emergency Call ×3, Stratos ×3, Miracle Ejector, Spirit of Neos) make the combo easy to start.
The deck is cheap to build and the new card is a reward from the in-game gate, no big boxes needed.
weaknesses: The wipe also destroys your own Set Spells and Traps, and only works when the opponent controls more cards than you.
Neos-based fusions made with Instant Contact need Neos on your field or in your Graveyard, or they cannot attack and lose their effects.
The skill limits you to Neos, Elemental HERO and Neo-Spacian Special Summons, and the first effect needs a Spirit of Neos or Miracle Ejector in hand.
Hand traps and negates on Polymerization or on Voltic Thunder slow the line (the creator answers with Super Polymerization).

horus.gamePlan: Horus is a very simple, bread-and-butter deck for the beginner: you play Spells that send your Horus monsters to the Graveyard, and they come back on their own while you control King's Sarcophagus. Start with Imsety, Walls of the Imperial Tomb or King's Sarcophagus, fill the field with Level 8 monsters, make Coach King Giantrainer (draw cards), then I:P Masquerena, and keep a Set Canopic Protector so you can bring a monster back and Link Summon on the opponent's turn. Each Horus monster also does something when the opponent removes one of your cards, so baiting their interaction is the plan. About half of the main deck is staples (hand traps and Kaijus), and the Extra Deck is the expensive part.
strengths: It is easy to play: the line is nearly the same every time and does not have long branches.
Your Horus monsters are protected from effects that do not target them and come back from the Graveyard, so it is hard to stop with one interruption.
Canopic Protector gives you plays on the opponent's turn, and the deck draws a lot of cards.
It is very strong in the current ranked meta and reaches King of Games easily.
weaknesses: Only 9 real starters, so hands without Imsety, Walls or King's Sarcophagus brick.

mathmech.gamePlan: Open with a Level 4 Mathmech Tuner (a small monster that lets you Synchro Summon) and use the skill to put the key monsters in your hand. Chain extra summons (an extender is a card that lets you summon more monsters) into Xyz and Link monsters (Xyz and Link are special monsters that live in the Extra Deck) that search, remove the opponent's cards, and draw. Finish with Geomathmech Final Sigma, a Level 12 monster that hits for double damage. When you search with the skill, take Circular and Diameter first, then Sigma, then Addition and Subtraction: keeping Sigma in your hand is safer than leaving it in the Graveyard, because a hand trap (a card the opponent plays from their hand) can stop it coming back, and Addition and Subtraction summon themselves from your hand, so they keep your follow-up going if you get interrupted. Because the skill gets you to your combo pieces, the rest of your deck goes to tech cards: hand traps and board breakers (cards that clear the opponent's board). Always check this guide's sources: the creators disagree on small details, and both mention a banlist change was coming when they recorded.
strengths: Out-resources opponents: the skill keeps adding monsters every turn, so you do not run out of cards early.
Several searches and a draw happen before the opponent can respond, which dodges some hand traps.
From turn 2 you can set a Mathmech trap and end the duel with Geomathmech Final Sigma.
weaknesses: Hand traps still hurt: D.D. Crow on the targets of Splash Mage's revive is very bad, and you are only protected against Effect Veiler and Infinite Impermanence for a short part of the combo.
In a long game the top decks (Vaalmonica, Branded, Snake-Eye) generate more resources than you do.
The deck leans heavily on tech cards, so a bad draw of tech cards makes it much weaker.
The Portuguese creator (Ignister) advises against building it right now because a banlist change and new decks were expected; check the current list before you spend gems.

memento.gamePlan: Memento is a combo deck: almost every card destroys or sends another, and each destruction triggers more effects. The goal is a field that is hard to break and a Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation (5000 ATK) that you can bring back every turn. Start with a starter (Mementotlan Angwitch, Mementotlan Dark Blade or Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo), use Mementotlan Fusion to make Mementomictlan Tecuhtlica - Creation King, destroy it for its effects, and finish with Combined Creation, Lyrilusc - Assembled Nightingale (a protective Xyz monster) and I:P Masquerena (a Link monster that turns into your negate on the opponent's turn). The creator says the deck has many lines and this video shows only the simplest; learn this one first, then add others from other creators. Do not pick up the deck and expect to master it quickly: the creator practised for more than 4 hours and still did not learn every play.
strengths: It fills your hand and Graveyard so fast that you can have 10 cards in hand by the end of the combo.
Almost everything protects itself: monsters come back from the Graveyard, and Lyrilusc - Assembled Nightingale makes sure you cannot lose the first turn.
On the opponent's turn you have several answers at once: Forbidden Droplet, Fracture Dance, Cranium Burst and I:P Masquerena into S:P Little Knight.
The creator says it has an answer to every kind of play and a clear way to win with Combined Creation attacking directly.
weaknesses: It is complex: you can lose games by playing the combo wrong or by running out of time while you learn.
D.D. Crow on Mementotlan Ghattic (or Bystial on a LIGHT or DARK Memento) ruins the main line, and Combined Creation is best protected in hand.

Combined Creation can be hit by a negate, a Dark Ruler No More or a banish; the creator says the only monster effect that matters to negate on his turn is Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo, Dark Blade or Angwitch.
The deck leans on tech cards (hand traps, selection-box cards) that depend on what you own.

scenarios.title: Turn 1 with Tatsunootoshigo in your hand: build Combined Creation and a protected field

skillPlan.note: The skill is step 1: it replaces a card from your hand with 2 new cards. In the replay he put Bone Party back.

start.note: The creator's opening hand (Tatsunootoshigo, Cranium Burst, Shleepy and Bone Party). Yours will differ: the same line works with other cards, and with Angwitch or Dark Blade you search or replace Tatsunootoshigo instead.

steps.when: Right at the start of your Main Phase
steps.needs: Any 1 card from your hand to put on the bottom of your deck (or send to the Graveyard). The creator returns Mementotlan Bone Party, because he can fetch it back later.
steps.gives: You draw 2 cards (3 if you are the second player on the first turn). Here you draw Mementotlan Goblin and Mementotlan Fracture Dance.
steps.reason: The skill turns a clumsy card into 2 new ones. The creator says that in this deck sending cards to the Graveyard is good too, and that it is best to send back a duplicate Level 1 or Level 3 monster.
Special Summon Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo from your hand. You can do this when you control no face-up monsters except Memento monsters, so do it before anything else is on your side of the field.

Destroy Tatsunootoshigo itself, then send Memento monsters with different names from your deck to the Graveyard, with Levels adding up to at most its own Level 5. In this line always send Mementotlan Ghattic (Level 2) and Mementotlan Shleepy (Level 3). Destroying a Memento monster this turn is what lets Shleepy come out later.
Ghattic was sent to the Graveyard by a Memento monster's effect, so it Special Summons itself. Then its effect adds a Memento card from your Graveyard to your hand: take Shleepy back.

A Memento monster was destroyed this turn, so Shleepy can Special Summon itself from your hand. When it is summoned it Fusion Summons a Memento Fusion monster using monsters from your hand or field: Mementotlan Twin Dragon, with Shleepy and Ghattic as the materials.

Because it was Fusion Summoned, Twin Dragon destroys itself and adds up to 2 Memento monsters with different names from your deck to your hand: Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation (your boss monster, kept in hand where a Dark Ruler No More or a hand trap cannot hit it) and Mementotlan Dark Blade.
Twin Dragon was destroyed, so it Special Summons a Level 6 or lower Memento monster from the Graveyard: Ghattic comes back.
Normal Summon Mementotlan Dark Blade. This is your only Normal Summon of the turn, so you cannot also search it with Tatsunootoshigo if you want it in hand later.
Dark Blade destroys a Memento monster you control (Ghattic) to Special Summon a Level 3 or lower Memento monster from your deck: Mementotlan Mace.
Mace destroys a Memento monster you control (Dark Blade) and adds any Memento card from your deck to your hand: take Mementotlan Fusion. If you already hold Fusion, search something else here.

Activate Mementotlan Fusion: Fusion Summon Mementomictlan Tecuhtlica - Creation King (Level 9) using Mementotlan Goblin from your hand and, because a Memento monster was destroyed this turn, Twin Dragon and Dark Blade from your Graveyard as extra materials (they go back to the Extra Deck and the deck).

Because Creation King was Fusion Summoned it sends 3 Memento cards from your deck or Extra Deck to the Graveyard: Mementotlan Dark Blade, Mementotlan Angwitch and Mementotlan Akihiron. These are all monsters you want in the Graveyard for later.

Banish Mementotlan Fusion from your Graveyard to destroy Creation King (a Memento monster you control), and add a Memento Spell/Trap to your hand: Mementotlan Bone Party. In the creator's words, the destroyed Creation King has already done its work and the destruction triggers more effects below.

A Memento monster you controlled was destroyed, so Mementotlan Akihiron Special Summons itself from the Graveyard. While it is on the field your Level 9 or higher Memento monsters can attack directly (the key to this deck's one-turn kills).
Banish Creation King from the Graveyard to add the Field Spell Mementomictlan to your hand. Because it waits in the Graveyard you do not need to rush to search the field.

Activate the Field Spell Mementomictlan. Your Memento monsters are protected from trap responses in battle, destroyed ones can come back, and each end phase it sets a Memento Spell/Trap from the Graveyard.

Activate Mementotlan Bone Party: destroy Akihiron and Special Summon a Memento monster with another name from your deck in Defense Position: Mementotlan Angwitch. Every destruction now sets off more effects.

Three effects trigger at once, so line them up as one chain: Angwitch adds a Memento monster from your deck (take Mementotlan-Horned Dragon); Akihiron adds a banished Memento card to your hand (take Mementotlan Fusion back); and the Field Spell Special Summons Mementotlan Goblin from the Graveyard to replace the destroyed Akihiron.

Goblin and Mace are two Level 1 monsters, so Xyz Summon Lyrilusc - Assembled Nightingale (Rank 1). On the opponent's draw you can detach a material to protect your Lyrilusc monsters, and you take no battle damage that turn. This is the creator's insurance against a bad turn.

You now have 3 or more Memento monsters with different names in the Graveyard, so Mementotlan-Horned Dragon Special Summons itself from your hand. Its destruction would also take down 2 of the opponent's cards.

Link Summon I:P Masquerena using Angwitch and Horned Dragon. On the opponent's turn you can use it to Link Summon S:P Little Knight (or a Knightmare Unicorn or Underworld Goddess of the Closed World) and remove a card.

Special Summon Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation (Level 11, 5000 ATK) by shuffling 5 Memento monsters with different names from your hand and Graveyard into the deck: Horned Dragon, Dark Blade, Angwitch, Tatsunootoshigo and Shleepy. With Akihiron gone you can no longer attack directly this turn, but you are building the opponent's-turn defence.

Set Cranium Burst, Fracture Dance and Mementotlan Fusion (your hand still holds one card). Combined Creation lets Cranium Burst negate monster effects 5 times by lowering its ATK, Fracture Dance destroys 2 cards, and Fusion can answer the opponent's turn. If you hold Forbidden Droplet, keep it in hand instead of setting Fusion.

scenarios.chainNotes: Keep Forbidden Droplet in hand if you have it and set the remaining Spell/Trap cards. Do not summon Combined Creation if it is in your hand together with Creation King and you have fewer than 3 different Memento monsters in the Graveyard. Mementotlan Shleepy and Mementotlan Ghattic are the cards you want to be hit by the opponent least, so the creator advises adapting if D.D. Crow lands on Ghattic.
scenarios.endBoard: Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation (5000 ATK) and Lyrilusc - Assembled Nightingale on the field with I:P Masquerena in the Extra Monster Zone, Mementomictlan active and Cranium Burst, Fracture Dance and Mementotlan Fusion set. One Shleepy stays in your hand.
scenarios.weakSpots: D.D. Crow on Mementotlan Ghattic breaks this line (you must find another route); a negate on the Fusion Summons or on Combined Creation's Special Summon slows you; and Combined Creation is not worth negating on the opponent's turn because its effect only revives a Memento, which is why the creator says to negate his starters instead.

Activate Mementotlan Bone Party: destroy Angwitch and Special Summon Mementotlan Dark Blade from your deck in Defense Position. Mementotlan-Horned Dragon can then Special Summon itself from your hand, because 3 Memento monsters with different names are in the Graveyard.

Set Mementotlan Fusion. At the end of the turn the Field Spell also sets Mementotlan Fracture Dance from the Graveyard for you, so you end with 2 Traps/Quick-Play cards ready for the opponent's turn. red-eyes.gamePlan: This is Red-Eyes Black Dragon updated to make two Red-Eyes Dark Dragoons on turn one, with a Despia and Bystial engine in the same deck. It needs a skill starter (Red-Eyes Black Dragon, Lord of the Red or Red-Eyes Transmigration) plus Aluber the Jester of Despia: the skill brings the ritual pieces and Meteor Dragon, Polymerization makes the first Dragoon with Dark Magician, and Aluber starts Branded Fusion and Albion, which makes the second Dragoon. You finish by Ritual Summoning Lord of the Red. Without Aluber you fall back on a Hieratic Seal, one Dragoon and Lord of the Red. The result is two omni-negates and a ritual monster that destroys Spells and Traps, about five or six interactions, plus 6 tech cards (Nibiru, Droll & Lock Bird and the Bystials) in the other slots.
strengths: Two Red-Eyes Dark Dragoons cannot be targeted or destroyed by card effects, and each negates once per turn: you are immune to most hand traps.
Lord of the Red destroys Spells and Traps, so it is very strong against decks with Continuous Spells and Traps, like Sarcophagus and Snake-Eye.
Even with a bad hand without Aluber you still get a decent board (a Dragoon, Lord of the Red and a Seal).
The deck keeps cards in hand and draws through Branded Regained and the Bystials.
weaknesses: The best line is a two-card combo: a skill starter plus Aluber. Without both you play the shorter lines.
There are only 15 slots outside the Red-Eyes cards, because the skill needs 15 Red-Eyes cards, so the deck has little room for extras.
Branded Fusion locks you to Fusion Monsters from the Extra Deck for the turn, so make the Dragoon and any other Extra Deck monster first.
The Dragoon's negate costs a discard, so you cannot spend your whole hand, and a Kaiju or Lava Golem can still remove it (Red-Eyes Spirit helps).

cards.name: Red-Eyes Black Dragon
cards.note: The Normal Monster the deck is built around. Reveal it to start the skill, use it as Fusion Material for Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon (with Dark Magician), and send it to the Graveyard as the cost of Red-Eyes Black Meteor Dragon. In the Graveyard it also pays for Red-Eyes Transmigration.

cards.name: Lord of the Red
cards.note: The Ritual boss (Level 8). Once per turn each, when a card or effect is activated it can destroy a monster on the field, and once per turn each it can destroy a Spell or Trap. The creator says it is extremely good against Continuous Spells and Traps. It is also one of the 3 cards you can reveal for the skill.

cards.name: Red-Eyes Transmigration
cards.note: Ritual Spell that Ritual Summons Lord of the Red. You Tribute monsters and/or banish Red-Eyes monsters from your Graveyard to reach Level 8, so a Level 4 monster plus a banished Red-Eyes monster is enough.

cards.name: Red-Eyes Insight
cards.note: Sends a Red-Eyes monster from your hand or deck to the Graveyard and adds a Red-Eyes Spell or Trap (not another Insight). It counts as one of the deck's 11 starters and is how you search Red-Eyes Spirit when your hand is already good. A third copy would fill a Red-Eyes slot, but the creator prefers the Trap because a dead Insight in a full hand does nothing.

cards.name: Red-Eyes Black Meteor Dragon
cards.note: Special Summons itself from your hand by sending a Level 5 or higher Normal Monster (like Red-Eyes Black Dragon) from your hand or deck to the Graveyard. That enables the second part of the skill, which needs a Red-Eyes monster on your side. From the Graveyard it can banish itself to add Red-Eyes Fusion. Tip from the creator: if you want a Normal Summon in the deck, you can swap one Meteor for a Red-Eyes monster you can Normal Summon that Insight can search; then you can still make Hieratic Seal if you are interrupted before the two Dragoons. He does not play it that way for now.

cards.name: Red-Eyes Spirit
cards.note: The 15th Red-Eyes card the skill needs, and a Trap that Special Summons a Red-Eyes monster from your Graveyard. If your Dragoon is hit by a Lava Golem or another removal, you bring it back. The creator picked it over a third Red-Eyes Insight because it adds an interaction.

substitutes.name: Red-Eyes Insight
substitutes.why: A third Red-Eyes Insight would also reach the 15 Red-Eyes cards. The creator did not use it because with a good hand it has nothing to search, and the Trap gives you an extra answer instead.

cards.name: Aluber the Jester of Despia
cards.note: The second combo piece with a starter. Normal Summon it to add a Branded Spell/Trap (Branded Fusion). If your Fusion Monster is destroyed or leaves the field by an opponent's effect, it Special Summons itself from the Graveyard and negates a monster, which counts as a hand-trap-style answer. A Level 4 body is also enough for the Ritual.

cards.name: Fallen of Albaz
cards.note: Fallen of Albaz is the Fusion Material for Albion the Branded Dragon. Branded Fusion sends it from your deck as material, and on its own it can discard a card to Fusion Summon when it is Summoned.

cards.name: Branded Fusion
cards.note: Branded Fusion Fusion Summons Albion the Branded Dragon from the Extra Deck using Fallen of Albaz and Bystial The Lubellion from your deck. While it is active you can only Special Summon Fusion Monsters from the Extra Deck, so make the Dragoon first.

cards.name: Branded in Red
cards.note: Quick-Play Spell that returns a Despia monster or Fallen of Albaz from your Graveyard and Fusion Summons a Level 8 or higher Fusion Monster. It works on the opponent's turn: you can make Guardian Chimera, Khaos Starsource Dragon or Despian Quaeritis.

substitutes.name: Branded Banishment
substitutes.why: The creator used Branded Banishment first, then swapped it for Branded in Red. Banishment is also an answer to Kaiju: if a Kaiju removes your Fusion Monsters, you activate it and recover them.

cards.name: Branded Regained
cards.note: Continuous Spell: when a LIGHT or DARK monster is banished, you put it on the bottom of the deck and draw 1, and when the opponent Summons a monster you can bring a Bystial back from the Graveyard. Every Ritual you do with banished Red-Eyes monsters turns into a draw.

cards.name: Branded Beast

cards.name: The Bystial Lubellion
cards.note: Special Summon it by Tributing a Level 6 or higher DARK Dragon (Albion works well). It can discard itself to search a Bystial, and it places a Branded Continuous Spell or Trap from your deck on the field. It is also a Level 8 LIGHT monster for Albion.

cards.name: Bystial Magnamhut
cards.note: Bystial: banish a LIGHT or DARK monster from a Graveyard to Special Summon it from your hand, as a Quick Effect when the opponent has a monster. At the End Phase it adds any Dragon. The creator counts the Bystials as hand traps, so the deck has 6 tech cards with Nibiru and Droll.

cards.name: Bystial Druiswurm

cards.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
cards.note: Stops decks that make many Summons in one turn, and is a powerful card in this meta.

cards.name: Droll & Lock Bird
cards.note: Stops the opponent's search turn. The creator notes that it also stops you from drawing, so with Droll in play he skips the Spell that draws and fetches the Trap directly.

substitutes.name: Branded Opening

It is a Quick-Play Spell that makes sure you have Aluber (you would have 6 Aluber with it), and while it is in the Graveyard it protects your Fusion Monsters from destruction by card effects. It is less flexible against hand-trap decks.

cards.name: Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon

It cannot be destroyed by card effects and cannot be targeted, it destroys monsters and burns for their ATK, and once per turn it discards a card to negate an activation and destroy that card (it is an omni-negate). Two of them mean two omni-negates that are hard to remove. Made with Dark Magician plus Red-Eyes Black Dragon or a Dragon Effect Monster.

cards.name: Albion the Branded Dragon

cards.name: Guardian Chimera

cards.name: Khaos Starsource Dragon

shining-sarcophagus.gamePlan: Shining Sarcophagus is a stalling and spell-based deck built around a Continuous Spell that monster effects cannot destroy. You reveal a Spellcaster (like Silent Magician Zero) for the skill, add the Sarcophagus and a monster that works with it, and then use cards that mention the Sarcophagus: Dark Magician and Gandora-G Special Summon themselves from your hand while it is on the field, Gadget Trio and Dark Magician Girl search it, and the Silent monsters grow and negate. The cards give you negates (Silent Magician Zero, Turn Silence, I:P Masquerena into S:P Little Knight, Number 90) while you hold the field. There are two builds from two videos: Build 1 (IgnisterPRC) opens with more search cards and Mulcharmy hand traps, and Build 2 (Sorem) leans on Dark Magician and Gandora-G with Lava Golem and Droll & Lock Bird. The Alternatives tab shows what changes and which cards you can swap.
strengths: The Sarcophagus cannot be destroyed by monster effects, and the Silent monsters negate effects that target it.
Plenty of negates and answers on both turns: spell negates, monster negates, hand traps and a Link chain into S:P Little Knight.
Both builds are easy to play and need few expensive cards: the structure decks give you most of the Spellcasters.
Gandora-G can clear the whole field in a turn when you need it, and the deck can still hit King of Games.
weaknesses: Spell/Trap removal on Shining Sarcophagus slows the whole deck, so keep a spare copy in hand as bait.
The skill needs a Spellcaster that mentions the Sarcophagus in your opening hand; Gandora-G and Dark Magician alone do not start it.
Several cards are situational (Dark Magical Curtain, Turn Silence), and a hand with too many of them can brick.
A Droll & Lock Bird on your first search stops the second one, and many decks play it right now.

cards.name: Shining Sarcophagus

Once per turn in your Main Phase it adds a card that mentions it, and when the opponent Special Summons from the Graveyard you discard a Spell to send that monster to the Graveyard. Build 1 plays 3, Build 2 plays 2.

It gains Levels (and 500 ATK per Level) when the opponent draws, and negates a Spell the opponent activates while you control Shining Sarcophagus. Both builds play 3. Build 1 says you could run fewer, but three are easier to find with the skill.

Its name is "Dark Magician" on the field, and if an effect destroys it while a Level 5 or higher monster is on the field it comes back and Sets a Spell/Trap that mentions Dark Magician. Build 1 plays 1, Build 2 plays 3, because it is a main piece of its Gandora line.

cards.name: Dark Magician Girl the Magician's Apprentice
cards.note: Special Summon it from your hand by discarding a card, and when it is summoned it adds Shining Sarcophagus. It gains 300 ATK for each monster that mentions the Sarcophagus in the Graveyards. Both builds play 2.

cards.name: Gandora-G the Dragon of Destruction

With Shining Sarcophagus on your side it Special Summons itself from your hand, and by paying half your Life Points it destroys and banishes every other card (the Sarcophagus is safe from monster effects), then Special Summons a Level 7 or lower monster that mentions the Sarcophagus with extra Levels. Both builds play 2. Build 1 says that with only one Gandora you can still play, because extra copies can brick.

cards.name: Gadget Trio

cards.note: Quick-Play Spell that Fusion Summons by shuffling Dark Magician or Dark Magician Girl into the deck (it is treated as The Eye of Timaeus), but the monster is banished at the end of the next turn. Both builds play 1.

cards.name: Ties That Bind
cards.note: With Shining Sarcophagus and a monster that mentions it, Special Summon up to 2 Level 4 or lower monsters with different names that mention it. After it resolves you cannot Special Summon from the Extra Deck this turn, so do your Extra Deck summons first. Only Build 1 plays it.

cards.name: Dark Magical Curtain
cards.note: Quick-Play Spell. Only Build 2 plays it. Build 1 says it is too specific and did not like it, and took it out of the deck. Build 2 uses it with Dark Magician for a Dark Magician Spell/Trap.

substitutes.name: Forbidden Droplet
substitutes.why: Build 1 says he would rather put a Forbidden Droplet, a Book of Moon or an Effect Veiler in this slot: the Curtain is too specific and the other cards are more useful turn after turn.

substitutes.name: Book of Moon
substitutes.why: Same advice as the Droplet: a Book of Moon is a general interaction, and the Curtain depends on a very specific line.

substitutes.name: Effect Veiler
substitutes.why: Effect Veiler is another general hand trap that the creator of Build 1 prefers to the Curtain.

cards.name: Mulcharmy Fuwalos
cards.note: Hand trap that draws a card each time the opponent Special Summons from the Deck or Extra Deck. Only Build 1 plays it. The creator says you do not need to copy his hand traps: he used what was available on his account.

cards.name: Mulcharmy Purulia
cards.note: Hand trap that draws a card each time the opponent Summons a monster from the hand. Only Build 1 plays it, 3 copies.

cards.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
cards.note: Stops decks that make many Summons in one turn. Build 1 plays 3, Build 2 plays 1.

cards.name: Droll & Lock Bird
cards.note: Hand trap that stops the opponent's search turn. Only Build 2 plays it (2 copies). Build 2 calls it the best card to hold back decks that search a lot.

cards.name: D.D. Crow
cards.note: Free hand trap from the structure deck that banishes a card from a Graveyard. Only Build 2 plays it (1 copy).

cards.name: Lava Golem
cards.note: Build 2 plays 3 Lava Golem to remove two monsters of the opponent from turn two onward, since your own Normal Summon is not needed. Build 2 says one-tribute Kaijus are a trade: Lava Golem is stronger, but it costs you 1000 damage each turn, and the Kaijus do not. Build 1 does not play it.

cards.name: Witch of the Black Forest
cards.note: Only Build 2 plays 1 Witch of the Black Forest, as its Normal Summon: when it goes to the Graveyard it adds a monster with 1500 or less DEF (here Droll & Lock Bird, D.D. Crow or Gadget Trio).

cards.name: Photon Jumper
cards.note: Only Build 2 plays 1 Photon Jumper: when the opponent's monster attacks, it ends the Battle Phase, and in the Graveyard it adds a Photon or Galaxy Spell/Trap (for Number 90).

cards.name: Dark Magician of Destruction
cards.note: Special Summoned from the Extra Deck in a turn you activated a Spell, by banishing a Level 6 or higher DARK Spellcaster (like Dark Magician Girl). Its name becomes Dark Magician, and it adds Dark Magician or a card that mentions it, such as The Eye of Timaeus or the Curtain. Both builds play it.

cards.name: Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon
cards.note: Fusion Summoned with The Gaze of Timaeus. It cannot be destroyed by effects or targeted and can negate. Both builds play it.

cards.name: Timaeus the United Magical Dragon
cards.note: Fusion Monster that Build 1 makes with The Eye of Timaeus. Only Build 1 plays it, in the slot where Build 2 plays Dingirsu and Number 68.

cards.name: Chaos Angel
cards.note: Synchro you can make with the Level 4 monsters, treating a DARK monster as a Tuner. When Special Summoned it banishes a card, and it gains protections from the Attributes of its materials. Both builds play it.

cards.name: Super Starslayer TY-PHON - Sky Crisis
cards.note: Rank 12 Xyz that Build 1 used as a last board breaker against a huge board. Only Build 1 plays it, and the creator says you may not need it.

cards.name: Number 90: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Lord
cards.note: Rank 8 that negates a monster effect by detaching a material. Both builds play it, and the creator of Build 2 says it is the best generic monster negate.

cards.name: Number 68: Sanaphond the Sky Prison
cards.note: Rank 8 that, once you detach a material, cannot be destroyed by card effects and stops both players from Special Summoning from the Graveyard until the end of the opponent's next turn. Only Build 2 plays it, because many decks (Horus, Memento, Branded, Snake-Eye) summon from the Graveyard.

cards.name: Dingirsu, the Orcust of the Evening Star
cards.note: Rank 8 that sends a card of the opponent's to the Graveyard when it is Special Summoned, without targeting, and protects your cards by detaching a material. Only Build 2 plays it.

cards.name: I:P Masquerena
cards.note: Link-2 made with two non-Link monsters. On the opponent's Main Phase it can Link Summon again, for example S:P Little Knight, and the Link monster made with it cannot be destroyed by the opponent's effects. Both builds play it.

cards.name: S:P Little Knight
cards.note: Link-2 made with I:P Masquerena, which banishes a card and can banish two monsters in response to an effect. Both builds play it.

substitutes.name: Knightmare Unicorn
substitutes.why: Both creators say that if you do not own S:P Little Knight you can use Knightmare Unicorn: it is also made with I:P, and it returns a monster on the opponent's field to their deck, but S:P is much stronger.

cards.name: Underworld Goddess of the Closed World
cards.note: Link-5 made with the opponent's monster as material. It negates the effects of the opponent's face-up monsters and negates a Special Summon from the Graveyard. Both builds play it.

steps.when: In your Main Phase (effect 2)
steps.needs: Reveal a Spellcaster monster that mentions Shining Sarcophagus from your hand. Here Dark Magician Girl the Magician's Apprentice.
steps.gives: Add up to 2 cards from your deck: Shining Sarcophagus and a monster that mentions it (here Silent Magician Zero).
steps.reason: It gets you the Sarcophagus and a monster that works with it, so you do not depend on drawing them. The skill is much better with three Silent Magician Zero in the deck.

steps.card: Dark Magician Girl the Magician's Apprentice
steps.reason: Special Summon Dark Magician Girl from your hand by discarding a card (here the spare Mulcharmy Fuwalos). When she is summoned she adds a second Shining Sarcophagus.

moves.card: Dark Magician Girl the Magician's Apprentice

steps.reason: Activate Shining Sarcophagus. Now Silent Magician Zero, Silent Swordsman Zero, Gandora-G and Dark Magician the Magician of Black Magic can use their effects. The second copy stays in your hand as bait for Spell/Trap removal.
In your Main Phase, use the Sarcophagus to add a card that mentions it from your deck: here Turn Silence, a Quick-Play Spell that negates a monster effect later.
Normal Summon Gadget Trio and add Ties That Bind (a Spell/Trap that mentions the Sarcophagus).

You activated a Spell this turn, so banish Dark Magician Girl (Level 6 DARK Spellcaster) to Special Summon Dark Magician of Destruction from the Extra Deck, and add The Eye of Timaeus or a card that mentions Dark Magician. Its name is Dark Magician on the field.

moves.card: Dark Magician Girl the Magician's Apprentice

scenarios.chainNotes: From here the creator makes I:P Masquerena with two non-Link monsters, then uses Ties That Bind to put Silent Magician Zero and Silent Swordsman Zero on the field and keeps S:P Little Knight for the opponent's turn (I:P Link Summons it in response). Do your Extra Deck summons first: Ties That Bind stops Extra Deck Special Summons for the rest of the turn. Keep Turn Silence and Future Silence in hand to answer a Spell or a monster effect.
scenarios.endBoard: Dark Magician of Destruction and Gadget Trio on the field with Shining Sarcophagus active, and Turn Silence, Ties That Bind and a second Sarcophagus in your hand: the creator then ends with I:P Masquerena, the Silent monsters and about six interactions.
scenarios.weakSpots: A hand without a Spellcaster that mentions the Sarcophagus cannot use the skill. Spell/Trap removal on Shining Sarcophagus stops the whole engine, which is why the creator keeps a spare copy. A hand-trap on Gadget Trio or Dark Magician Girl slows the search.

Pay half your Life Points: Gandora-G destroys and banishes every other card it can (the Sarcophagus is safe from monster effects), then Special Summons Gadget Trio from your deck with its Level raised by the number of destroyed cards. Dark Magician is the card that is destroyed here.

In the next steps of his line he uses Dark Magician of Destruction (banishing a Level 6+ DARK Spellcaster) to add Dark Magical Curtain, then makes Number 90 with the Level 8 monsters, I:P Masquerena and S:P Little Knight.
